key_insight: HSE introduced a practical screened-hybrid strategy that made exact exchange affordable for solids and unexpectedly delivered much better semiconductor band gaps than semilocal density functionals.
engineering_relevance: Accurate, transferable band-gap predictions improve defect physics, photovoltaics, power electronics, and quantum-information materials screening.
method: Use short-range exact exchange with long-range screening to make hybrids tractable in extended systems.
Keep the 25% exact-exchange fraction inherited from molecular PBE hybrids rather than fitting it to solids.
Compare HSE03/HSE06 and newer semilocal, meta-GGA, and dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals against solid benchmarks.
evidence_signal: The abstract says HSE band gaps for ordinary semiconductors and selected oxides came out substantially closer to experiment, and recent comparisons benchmark band gaps alongside structures, energetics, cost, and transferability.
watch_item: Fixed screening and fixed exchange fractions can limit transferability across materials, so tuned or dielectric-dependent variants may be needed for some solids.
paper_title: Perspective: The HSE Screened Hybrid and the Band Gap Problem: Origins, Impact, and the Contenders
